context: Request: general litigation matters that involved a retained damages expert, and the documents showing each engagement. Rubric: ten matters (1005-00005, 1010-00005, 1011-00004, 1012-00005, 1021-00006, 1022-00005, 1033-00006, 1034-00003, 1038-00007, 1044-00006), each with an expert and proof-document criterion (16 criteria), plus a precision criterion (one more matter, not named in the log, is permitted).

stages.note: Store-wide extraction script for expert and damages phrases with snippets; times out after about 930K characters. The summary lists about a dozen candidate matters; the review flags the partial output and boilerplate hits.

stages.note: declared: Scan document text with an extraction script (attempt 2). find | grep over all paths for expert, damages and retention file names (204 files saved), but prints only the lines for the dozen matters named after the scan. The review flags that filter.

stages.note: Lists all files of six of those matters and reads one further document (closing memo, status report, report) from eleven.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents

runs.failure_point: Its file-name search for expert-retention files was printed only for the matters its timed-out scan had named, so five needed matters never entered the candidate set; the answer also asserts nine other matters.

first_error.stage: Search file names for request keywords
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review named the filter to a fixed set of matters.
first_error.why: The find over all paths saved 204 expert-related file names, but the agent printed only lines for the dozen matters named after the timed-out scan, so needed matters whose retention letters were in that list (and one the scan itself had shown) were never seen or opened; the stage review flagged this fixed-matter filter and the agent went straight to reading.

other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) Reviews warned about thin, one-letter verification; only one of the nine (verified through a declaration) was named.
other_errors.why: The answer lists nine matters outside the qualifying set, including a sibling matter of a needed one, each judged from one retention letter or declaration; the reviews warned about unopened candidates and thin verification but did not name these inclusions (evidence seen at [26]-[76]).

runs.failure_point: Its text scan listed all ten needed matters, but it never opened two of them, and its answer excluded three it had opened on the strength of one expert letter each, while asserting ten other matters.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) The review warned about many surfaced matters left unopened, with examples that did not include the two skipped.
first_error.why: The tight scan just before listed every needed matter, but of the roughly 25 matters it chose to read it left out two of them, which never entered the answer; the review warned about unopened surfaced matters only with examples that did not include them.

other_errors.why: Three needed matters it had opened are excluded or omitted: in each it read a letter for a different (non-damages) expert or a memo recommending retention and judged the matter from that one document (evidence seen at [45]-[79]); no review named these exclusions.

other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) 'Possible over-inclusion' and a request to check each entry for an executed engagement.
other_errors.why: The answer asserts ten matters outside the qualifying set; the write review flagged possible over-inclusion and asked for each engagement to be checked, and the agent downgraded only one matter to a proposal.

runs.failure_point: One needed matter has no expert-named files and was never reached because the agent stopped its full-text scan while it was still running; the answer also excludes an opened matter as pre-filing and asserts six other matters.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) Two reviews named the full-text scan as still running when the agent moved on.
first_error.why: Its other searches were limited to expert-named files; the background full-text scan that could reach the remaining matter was abandoned while still running, and after the review flagged this the agent polled once more and drafted anyway, so that matter never surfaced.

other_errors.why: It read the needed matter's retention letter for a damages expert but excluded the matter because the letter describes litigation not yet filed (evidence seen at [58]-[68]); the write review flagged over-inclusion instead.

other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) 'Over-inclusion risk' naming only the proposed-expert entry.
other_errors.why: The answer asserts six matters outside the qualifying set; after the write review flagged over-inclusion risk the agent moved two proposed engagements to conditional leads but kept the others.

divergence: All three runs failed, each by both omitting needed matters and asserting many others (precision failed in all three). They failed at different stages. T0 ran a store-wide file-name search for expert-retention files that likely reached most needed matters but displayed only the matters its timed-out text scan had already named, so five never entered the candidate set (over-narrow filter, flagged by the critic and ignored). T1's tight text scan surfaced all ten, but its screening reads skipped two of them and its answer excluded three it had opened, judging from one expert letter each (surfaced, not opened). T2 got closest (12/17): an extraction script over expert-named files reached nine of ten, but the one matter without expert-named files needed a full-text scan, which the agent stopped while it was still running after the critic had flagged that (search miss); it also excluded one opened matter as pre-filing. In every run the reviews repeated generic 'many surfaced matters unopened' warnings, and the over-inclusion flags led at most to downgrading one or two matters.
